extensions.note: theme.css declares a light :root ramp and a .dark override. index.html hardcodes class="dark" on <html> and nothing toggles it, so the darkValue below is what actually renders today. The frontmatter in DESIGN.md carries the light :root values as the normative token declaration.

primary.purpose: The commit action, the decided state, and your own voice in chat. The scarcest colour on any screen.

primary-container.purpose: Resting 'I'm In' vote button, confirmed-date chip in the week strip, loading mark.

secondary.purpose: The 'Maybe' vote. Desaturated to near-neutral so it reads as adjacent to green without competing.

secondary-container.purpose: Resting 'Maybe' button, 'Confirmed' status chip, and the active pill behind the bottom-nav icon.

tertiary.purpose: The only hue outside the green family. Means 'voting is still open' and must never be mistaken for confirmed.

tertiary-container.purpose: 'Voting Phase' status chip and proposal days in the week strip.

error.purpose: 'Can't', 'Cancelled', and the unread-invite dot. Never form validation styling on its own.

surface.purpose: The page. Faintly green-tinted rather than pure white or black, so accents never look pasted on.

on-surface.purpose: Primary text — titles, values, anything countable.

on-surface-variant.purpose: Secondary text, metadata rows, inactive icons, leading icons in detail lists. Passes 4.5:1 in both ramps (9.2:1 light, 10.1:1 dark) — a legitimate text colour, not a whisper.

surface-container-low.purpose: Standard list-card background. WARNING: in the dark ramp this equals --surface exactly, so cards using it have zero tonal separation from the page and survive on shadow alone. Prefer surface-container or higher.

outline.purpose: Text-field strokes and the resting border of an open vote option card.

outline-variant.purpose: The global divider colour and the border of a losing vote option.

display.purpose: Declared in the scale, not currently used. Available for a genuine hero moment.

title.purpose: App-bar greeting, panel titles, the date numeral in the week strip.

title-md.purpose: Section headers and game-card titles. The most consequential role in the system — how a scanning user finds their game.

body.purpose: Text-field input and label text, empty-state headlines. The 16px floor also prevents iOS zoom-on-focus.

body-md.purpose: Every metadata row — date, time, location, chat message text.

label.purpose: All button text, 'View all' links, player counts.

label-md.purpose: Status chips, vote-button labels, nav item labels, vote tallies.

shadows.name: md3-1
shadows.purpose: Resting elevation for game cards and filled buttons. The default when something needs to lift at all. 29 uses — by far the dominant token.

shadows.name: md3-5
shadows.purpose: Floating chrome — sticky action bars and elements overlaying scrolling content.

motion.name: ease-md3-emphasized
motion.purpose: Default emphasized easing for state transitions.

motion.name: ease-md3-emphasized-decelerate
motion.purpose: Entrances. Vote option cards enter on this curve over 0.4s, staggered 60ms per index.

motion.name: ease-md3-standard
motion.purpose: Standard easing for small state changes.

motion.name: duration-state-layer
motion.purpose: State-layer opacity fade on hover and press, and text-field border/label transitions.

motion.name: duration-default
motion.purpose: The dominant transition duration across the app (transition-colors on buttons, chips, nav).

motion.name: duration-progress
motion.purpose: Step-progress bar fill in the create-game wizard.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: All animation and transition durations collapse to this under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, set globally in tailwind.css.

breakpoints.name: base
breakpoints.purpose: The app shell's max width. The only layout that exists — design at this width.

breakpoints.name: sm
breakpoints.purpose: Above this the shell widens to max-w-lg (512px). No layout changes, only more breathing room.

components.name: Filled Button

components.name: Vote Button
components.description: The signature control. Three sit side by side at equal width — I'm In, Maybe, Can't. Unselected sits in its container tone with a solid 2px border; selected inverts to the solid role colour. Each shows its own running count.
components.css: .ds-vote-row { display: flex; gap: 8px; } .ds-vote { flex: 1; display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; gap: 4px; min-height: 48px; padding: 10px 0; border-radius: 12px; border: 2px solid; cursor: pointer; font-family: Roboto, sans-serif; transition: background-color 0.2s, color 0.2s, border-color 0.2s; } .ds-vote-label { font-size: 12px; font-weight: 500; line-height: 1; letter-spacing: 0.5px; } .ds-vote-count { font-size: 11px; font-weight: 500; line-height: 1; letter-spacing: 0.5px; opacity: 0.8; } .ds-vote--in { background: var(--primary-container, #ADF3B0); color: var(--on-primary-container, #002106); border-color: var(--primary, #2D7A3A); } .ds-vote--in.ds-vote--active { background: var(--primary, #2D7A3A); color: var(--on-primary, #FFFFFF); border-color: transparent; } .ds-vote--maybe { background: var(--secondary-container, #D5E8CF); color: var(--on-secondary-container, #111F0F); border-color: var(--secondary, #52634F); } .ds-vote--maybe.ds-vote--active { background: var(--secondary, #52634F); color: var(--on-secondary, #FFFFFF); border-color: transparent; } .ds-vote--out { background: var(--error-container, #FFDAD6); color: var(--on-error-container, #410002); border-color: var(--error, #BA1A1A); } .ds-vote--out.ds-vote--active { background: var(--error, #BA1A1A); color: var(--on-error, #FFFFFF); border-color: transparent; } .ds-vote:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px color-mix(in srgb, var(--primary, #2D7A3A) 50%, transparent); }

components.name: Status Chip
components.description: The visual contract of the game lifecycle. Four mappings that must not be reassigned: Voting Phase to tertiary, Confirmed to secondary, Completed to surface-variant, Cancelled to error.

narrative.northStar: The Group Chat With a Scoreboard
narrative.overview:
OptIn looks like somewhere friends talk and behaves like somewhere a decision gets made. The surface language is warm, low-ceremony, tonal — rounded containers in soft greens and greys, nothing that reads as enterprise software or as a league management console. But underneath every screen there is a running tally, and the interface never lets you forget it. 7 In. 7/10 players. Option 2 — Winner. 3 spots left. The product's entire substance is quantities a group can act on, so the design's job is to keep those quantities in front of people while making the act of contributing to them feel like tapping a message, not filing a form.

The system is Material Design 3, implemented properly rather than approximated. That is not a default; it is the committed language, and the codebase honours it more thoroughly than most M3-flavoured products do — the full tonal role set, the real type scale with per-role letter-spacing, ripple-equivalent state layers as ::after overlays at 8% hover and 12% pressed, the seven-step shape scale, M3's emphasized and standard easing curves. Depth comes from tone before it comes from shadow. A card is a different surface tone, not a floating slab.

Green carries a specific meaning here and it is not 'brand.' Green is the colour of consensus reached. Turf Green fills the button that commits you, the border of the option that won, the dot on a confirmed date, the bubble of the message you sent. Teal-tertiary means still deciding. Muted olive-secondary means maybe. Red-error means can't and cancelled. The palette is a state machine, and using an accent decoratively breaks the one thing the user is reading the screen for.

The rejections are just as load-bearing. This product was once styled as iOS Liquid Glass — translucent white cards, backdrop-blur, iOS system blue #007AFF, .ios-card. That world was replaced deliberately and only fragments remain. Glassmorphism, blur-based depth, and iOS system colour are anti-references, not options. So is decorative sport imagery inside decision UI: hero photography exists per sport, but it never sits behind a vote.
keyCharacteristics: Tonal-first depth: surface containers do the layering, shadows only lift what floats
The palette is a state machine — every accent is a game state, never decoration
Pill and rounded-rectangle geometry throughout; no hard corners anywhere
Counts are visible at rest, never behind a tap
430px phone viewport is the only layout; there is no desktop composition
Roboto at 500 does almost all the work — weight is hierarchy, not size

rules.name: The State Machine Rule
rules.body: Every accent colour in this system means a game state: green is decided, teal is deciding, olive is maybe, red is refused. Using an accent for emphasis, decoration, or variety puts a lie on the screen. If a thing is not a game state, it is a neutral.

rules.name: The One Commit Rule
rules.body: At most one filled-primary control is visible per card and per screen region. If two things on a card are both filled green, neither reads as the commitment.

rules.name: The Tonal Separation Rule
rules.body: A card must differ from what it sits on by at least one step of the surface-container ramp. In the dark ramp --surface, --background, and --surface-container-low are all #1A1C19, so GameCard's bg-surface-container-low has zero tonal separation from the page and survives on shadow-md3-1 alone. That is a defect to fix, not a pattern to copy — reach for surface-container or higher when a card must read as a card in the shipped theme.

rules.name: The Countable Emphasis Rule
rules.body: Any number a user acts on — vote tally, roster count, spots left, cost each — is set at 500 minimum and never at Label Small. Numbers are this product's content; they do not get the timestamp treatment.

rules.name: The Sixteen Floor Rule
rules.body: Interactive text inputs are Body Large (16px) and never smaller, on every screen, without exception. Below 16px iOS zooms the viewport on focus and breaks the fixed 430px layout.

rules.name: The Uppercase Exception
rules.body: All-caps appears exactly once, on the GAME INVITE eyebrow in the notifications panel, at Label Small with tracking-wider. It is an eyebrow label, not a style. Do not uppercase buttons, chips, section headers, or nav labels — M3 does not, and this system does not.

rules.name: The Thumb Reach Rule
rules.body: Every interactive element is at least 48x48px, including elements that only look smaller — the 40px notification bell is wrapped to min-w-[48px] min-h-[48px], and inline text links get min-h-[48px]. 48 is the floor, not 44.

rules.name: The Tone-Before-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Before adding a shadow, ask whether a step on the surface-container ramp says the same thing. It usually does, and it survives the dark ramp better. Shadows on a #1A1C19 background are nearly invisible; tone is not.

rules.name: The No Blur Rule
rules.body: No backdrop-filter, no translucent-white surfaces, no glass. Exactly one backdrop-blur-sm survives in the codebase, in StatusBar.tsx, and it is a leftover from the replaced iOS Liquid Glass identity. Depth is tone and shadow. Nothing here is frosted.

rules.name: The Pill-or-Card Rule
rules.body: If it performs an action or labels a state, it is fully rounded. If it contains content, it takes 12px or 16px. There is no third shape.

rules.name: The Two-Pixel Decision Rule
rules.body: A 2px border means a choice lives here. Use it for vote controls and for the option that won; do not spend it on decoration, because it is the strongest non-colour signal the system has.

dos: Do use the MD3 token utilities for everything: bg-surface-container-low, text-on-surface-variant, rounded-md3-large, shadow-md3-1, text-title-md. theme.css is the only source of truth for colour, type, shape and elevation.
Do treat accent colour as game state — green decided, teal deciding, olive maybe, red refused — and reach for a neutral whenever the thing being coloured is not a game state.
Do reach for a surface-container step before reaching for a shadow, and verify the result against the dark ramp, since that is the ramp that ships.
Do give every interactive element a 48x48px minimum target, wrapping visually smaller controls in min-w-[48px] min-h-[48px] rather than growing them.
Do keep interactive text at Body Large (16px) so iOS does not zoom the viewport on focus.
Do use md3-state-surface / md3-state-primary for interaction feedback, and transition-colors for state changes.
Do centre fixed elements with left-1/2 -translate-x-1/2 inside the 430px shell.
Do put secondary surfaces in a bottom sheet over the current screen rather than routing away from the game the user is looking at.
Do keep the counts visible at rest — tallies, 7/10 players, spots left, cost each. They are the content.
Do clean up drift when you touch a file. The known sites are listed in the don'ts; each is a small, safe, local fix.
donts: Don't introduce raw Tailwind palette colours. Current violations to migrate: the offline / session-expired / demo banners in Layout.tsx:48-80 (bg-gray-900, bg-rose-50, bg-amber-50), the tie-break panel in GameViewScreen.tsx:1297-1361 (twelve amber-* utilities), and the demo-mode row in ProfileScreen.tsx:243-259. Every one of these has an exact token equivalent — inverse-surface, error-container, tertiary-container.

Don't ship iOS system blue. #007AFF survives as the default profile colour in AuthContext.tsx:44, four times in ChatsScreen.tsx, and as theme_color in both index.html and public/manifest.json — where it sets the browser and install-prompt chrome to a competitor's brand colour. It is a leftover from the replaced identity, not a token.

Don't mix raw Tailwind radii into token-styled screens. rounded-xl / rounded-3xl appear roughly forty times in GameViewScreen.tsx and ProfileScreen.tsx alongside rounded-md3-*, producing 12px and 16px radii that look right by luck and drift on any scale change. Use rounded-md3-medium and rounded-md3-large.
Don't use glassmorphism, backdrop-filter, or translucent white cards. That identity was replaced; the surviving backdrop-blur-sm in StatusBar.tsx is debt.
Don't import design tokens from constants/md3.ts. It exports a blue-primary M3 palette that contradicts theme.css on every colour role. It is stale and will silently produce off-brand UI.
Don't raise elements on hover or add hover:shadow-*. State layers handle interaction; elevation is static.
Don't uppercase buttons, chips, section headers, or nav labels. The single all-caps eyebrow in the notifications panel is the exception that defines the rule.
Don't put more than one filled-primary button in a card or screen region.

Don't carry the shadcn/ui vocabulary in components/ui/ into app screens. Those files are stock Radix wrappers using rounded-md, rounded-lg and their own colour variables; they are not the OptIn system. MUI and Emotion are installed and unused — do not start using them.
Don't hardcode dates or times. Every displayed date derives from real timestamps.
Don't rely on colour alone to distinguish In / Maybe / Can't. Each vote control carries an icon and a text label for exactly this reason; keep all three.
